title: Aurora - Escalation Postmortem and Reliability Plan
summary: Postmortem walk-through for the 2027-03-11 degradation affecting inference latency & tail errors. Reviewed root cause hypotheses (autoscaler config + KV cache invalidation), mitigation steps taken, and agreed reliability improvements and runbook updates.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're on the record. Today is the Aurora escalation postmortem follow-up, thanks for making time.
[00:22] Marco (Head of Platform): Thanks Maya. Appreciate you folks pulling this together. We want to make sure we're aligned on next steps and the permanant fixes.
[00:40] Daniel (Redwood SE): Hi all, Daniel here. I'll run through the timeline we sent earlier and we can dig into open q's. Apologies if the automated transcript mangled some names in the deck, there were a couple of typos.
[01:05] Hannah (SRE): No worries. We mostly care about what happened at 03/11 03:14 UTC — we saw latency spikes and a bunch of 5xx tail errors.
[01:25] Priya (CSM): I can confirm the account team got the initial incident email and the SLO / SLA thresholds you shared were the trigger thresholds.
[01:40] Daniel (SE): Right. Quick refresher: at 03/11 ~03:14 we observed an autoscaler thrash—two scale events within 90s—combined with a KV-cache invalidation flood that caused a large number of cold KV misses. That increased token generation latency and pushed requests over the retry/exhaust thresholds which produced the 5xx counts.
[02:10] Sophie (Security): Quick Q on data plane — were any customer payloads routed to a fallback model or outside your VPC during the event? We need notes for our audit.
[02:28] Maya (AE): No, Sophie, nothing left the configured private deployment. All requests stayed in your VPC; we did fallback on a lower-capacity model variant within the same private pool for about 8 minutes.
[02:45] Ethan (Product): I guess the big question is why the autoscaler overshot. Were there mis-set thresholds, or was it request burstiness?
[03:05] Daniel (SE): We're seeing correlation with a spike in concurrent long-sequence requests from a batch job you kicked off (we have the logs). The scaler reacted to a CPU-based metric with a 30s window; that metric spiked because KV cache misses amplified per-request compute. So two causes: external workload pattern and a conservative scaler cooldown.
[03:40] Marco (Head of Platform): So it's two fold — customer batch + config. What's the permanent fix?
[03:50] Daniel (SE): Short term we tightened the cooldown and added a request-count based metric. Medium term: we propose improving prefix/KV caching heuristics (we call it prefix cache or KV cache) and a per-deployment warmup path for scheduled batch jobs.
[04:20] Hannah (SRE): Any timeline for the KV cache heuristics? This one bit us hard.
[04:30] Maya (AE): Daniel, can you speak to schedule?
[04:35] Daniel (SE): Sure. We have a patch in staging that changes cache invalidation batching and reduces thrash. If tests pass, we can push to prod next week (target 2027-03-24). We'll also add pre-warm hooks so scheduled jobs can call a prewarm endpoint.
[05:00] Sophie (Security): From a compliance perspective we also need the incident timeline, the audit logs, and the exact fallback behavior documented.
[05:12] Priya (CSM): We'll share the incident timeline and the raw metric charts extracted from the console. Maya will include the fallback variant names and the exact minutes of the fallback.
[05:30] Marco: We also noticed higher token costs during that window — can you confirm charge-back calculations and any credits for reduced availability?
[05:45] Maya: We flagged the usage team, we'll share a pro-rated credit proposal in the follow-up. We'll include cutout minutes and the impacted routes.
[06:00] Ethan: Ok good. On runbooks — our oncall hit the alert but manual steps were slow. Any plan to automate mitigation?
[06:15] Daniel: Yes. We're adding an automated mitigation to temporarily pin incoming batched routes to a dedicated warm pool when concurrent long-sequence patterns are detected. Also an optional rate-limit rule you can enable per-route.
[06:35] Hannah: Will that require infra changes on our side?
[06:40] Daniel: Minimal. We will coordinate a short config flip (one line) and a flag in the Console. We can test in your staging before enabling.
[06:55] Sophie: Also, please confirm KMS usage during the event. We need to know whether any key operations failed.
[07:05] Daniel: No KMS failures. Keys were available. The failure mode was compute-side, not crypto.
[07:18] Marco: You mentioned KV cache invalidation flood — what triggered the invalidation?
[07:25] Daniel: Looks like your deployment used a config that invalidates cache on code push; a CI job pushed a rollback which triggered invalidation across pods. Combined with the batch job, that caused many cold starts.
[07:50] Marco: Oof — we need to change that trigger. Our CI team can avoid wide invalidation during heavy batch windows.
[07:58] Maya: We'll document recommended CI gating practices in the best-practices doc we share.
[08:10] Ethan: Can Redwood put a short circuit so invalidations only happen on canary and then roll out?
[08:20] Daniel: Yep, we have a canary-first invalidation flow; we need to enable it for your org and add the guardrails. We will send an enablement guide.
[08:35] Hannah: About alerts — the threshold was hit but it wasn't actionable quickly. What can be tuned?
[08:42] Daniel: Two things: reduce alert noise by creating a composite alert (latency + error rate + cache-miss ratio) and shorten the evaluation window for critical SLO alerts to capture fast-moving incidents. We'll propose specific thresholds.
[09:05] Priya (CSM): I'll run the proposed alert changes by your oncall and schedule a staging test.
[09:12] Marco: Good. Anything on observability we should add?
[09:18] Maya: We'll add per-route KV-miss histograms, token-level tail latency, and a trace example. Expect those in the shared dashboard by end of week.
[09:40] Sophie: For our audit we need a timeline of who touched what in the private control plane — can you provide admin audit logs?
[09:50] Daniel: Yes, we'll export the control plane audit logs for the 24 hour window and redact as needed.
[10:00] Ethan: There was some discussion about dedicated capacity vs hosted — any recommendation after this event?
[10:10] Daniel: Dedicated gives you predictable capacity and isolates noisy neighbors; it doesn't solve client-side CI invalidation. For heavy scheduled batch workloads, dedicated reserved pool with pinned model variants and prewarm hooks is the cleanest option.
[10:32] Marco: Cost vs reliability tradeoff then. We'll run ROI internally.
[10:40] Maya: We'll help with a cost model and a one-week dedicated pilot if you want to trial.
[10:52] Hannah: Can we get a small bench test that simulates our 2-hour nightly batch?
[10:58] Daniel: Yes — we'll schedule a dedicated bench on a smaller pool, run with your sequences, and show KV-miss curves. Need your logs and a sample payload.
[11:12] Marco: I'll have the CI team and SRE send sample payloads to Priya by EOD.
[11:22] Priya: Got it.
[11:28] Sophie: A question about rollback policy: during the event you mentioned a fallback to lower-capacity model variant. Did that happen automatically?
[11:38] Daniel: Yes, we have an automatic fallback policy that triggers when per-route errors exceed threshold. It chose a compatible quantized variant in the same pool; the output quality was slightly degraded but service continued. We'll surface the variant IDs in the follow-up.
[11:58] Ethan: We need to test the fallback quality – product wants to see example outputs.
[12:05] Maya: We'll include 3 example transcripts comparing primary vs fallback outputs.
[12:14] Marco: For the runbook updates, who will own the doc?
[12:20] Priya: Redwood will draft the updates; Aurora owns internal steps. We'll do a joint review.
[12:30] Maya: Action items: Daniel will produce the technical write-up; I will collate timeline, credits, and next steps. Priya will coordinate tests.
[12:46] Hannah: Sounds good. A couple of nitty extras — is there a plan to reduce token cost spikes during fallback?
[12:55] Daniel: We'll tune batching and token limits per-route to reduce cost; also the prewarm reduces cold miss cost.
[13:05] Marco: Anything else on compliance?
[13:10] Sophie: Just the audit bundle and the fallback doc.
[13:18] Maya: We'll aim to have the follow-up package by 2027-03-20.
[13:25] Ethan: And we'll reconvene in the follow-up call to sign off on runbook changes.
[13:32] Priya: Scheduling note — the follow-up call is proposed 2027-03-25 15:00 UTC. I'll send the invite.
[13:45] Maya: Any final questions?
[13:50] Marco: No, good summary. Thanks team.
[13:55] Daniel: Thanks all — we'll be in touch with the package.
[14:00] Maya: End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: speaker overlaps occasionally masked, some proper nouns (KV cache, rockford?) may be transcribed imperfectly. Timestamps approximate every 20-60s to match meeting flow.
